title: operator-orchestrator-timeout-marking-nodes-tainted-and-causing-config-drift
creator: Aisha Chen
body:
Summary: During a customer-driven private cluster upgrade, the operator orchestrator hit a reconciliation timeout while waiting for post-upgrade webhook validation. The operator entered an error path that tainted a subset of nodes and triggered an aggressive drain flow for pods that relied on KV cache state. This left customer inference fleets degraded for ~22 minutes and caused configmap annotation divergence between Helm release state and live CRs.

Observed behavior:
- Helm upgrade applied new operator image and CRD changes; post-upgrade mutatingwebhook check blocked for >2m due to a slow readiness probe on node-agent.
- The operator orchestrator loop timed out waiting for webhook sync and flipped a safety-state that taints nodes with "redwood/operator-unsafe-upgrade=true" and initiated eviction by calling the drain controller.
- Evictions raced with existing KV cache writes resulting in partial cache flush and schema-skewed k/v entries on two nodes.
- Helm release status reported UpgradeSucceeded while live CR status showed "reconciling (stalled)".

Immediate impact:
- Two enterprise customers reported 5xx errors from hosted endpoints mapped to private clusters (high customer impact).
- Automated alerts fired (upgrade-duration > 10m) and PagerDuty engagement occurred.

Root cause (investigation summary):
- Orchestrator timeout path is non-idempotent: when webhook sync fails, the operator marked nodes as unsafe and called drain without a compensating check for KV-cache-consistency.
- Leader-election lease duration defaulted to a value too close to our readiness probe window; transient probe delays (network jitter) caused unnecessary failover semantics.
- Helm post-upgrade hooks do not validate KV schema compatibility before removing old controller pods.

Mitigation performed (customer-facing runbook actions):
1) Reverted in-place operator upgrade for affected clusters using Helm rollback (--atomic) for quick restorative state.
2) Manually removed taint "redwood/operator-unsafe-upgrade=true" from affected nodes to reallow scheduling.
3) Triggered a KV schema reconciliation job (ad-hoc script) to rehydrate missing keys and reconcile inconsistent versions.
4) Opened support ticket with customers, provided RCA timeline and mitigation steps; issued credits per SLA for affected windows.

Code fixes proposed in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-operator/pull/1234
Changes in PR: increase leader-election lease to 45s, make orchestrator timeout path idempotent (guarded drain), add preflight KV-schema-check hook in Helm chart, add upgrade watchdog that aborts upgrade and triggers automatic rollback if post-upgrade checks exceed 6m.

Tests and validation planned:
- Add e2e upgrade test matrix that injects delayed readiness probes and network latency to the operator and node-agent.
- Add unit tests for idempotent drain behavior and explicit KV-schema compatibility checks.
- Add telemetry events for upgrade start/finish/duration and for any automatic rollback decision.

Follow-ups and process changes: 
- Update on-prem upgrade runbook to include a pre-upgrade KV-schema snapshot and post-upgrade verification checklist.
- Create a Console dashboard tile for private upgrade durations and aggregated helm post-upgrade hook failures.
- Schedule a retro with SE and support teams to refine communication and automated mitigation thresholds.
